results.name: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Lateral Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and lie on your side with your lower arm resting on the bench. Hold a dumbbell with your upper hand, arm extended at your side with your palm facing your body.
Raise the dumbbell up in an arc motion until your arm is straight at shoulder level.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other side.
tips: Exhale as you lift the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
Hold the bench edge with your free hand to support your body during the exercise.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the movement to reduce strain on the joint.
results.description: Dumbbell Incline One Arm Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Incline Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and lie chest-first against it, allowing your arms to hang down with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other.
Raise both arms out to the sides until they are at shoulder height, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the top of the movement, ensuring your arms are parallel to the floor and in line with your shoulders.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep a slight bend in your elbows throughout the exercise to protect your joints.
Ensure your wrists remain straight and aligned with your forearms.
Select a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise.
results.description: Dumbbell Incline Rear Lateral Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Incline Shrug
instructions: Set an incline bench to a 45-degree angle and sit back against it, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms extended at your sides, palms facing each other.
Shrug your shoulders upward, lifting the dumbbells towards your ears, without bending your elbows.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you shrug your shoulders upward and inhale as you lower them.
Focus on lifting your shoulders straight up and down, avoiding any circular or forward motion.
Use a slow and controlled motion to maximize muscle engagement and avoid swinging.
results.description: Dumbbell Incline Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Kneeling Arnold Press
instructions: Begin by kneeling on the floor with your knees shoulder-width apart. Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing your body and your elbows bent and facing down.
Rotate your palms forward as you press the dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended.
Reverse the motion, lowering the dumbbells back to shoulder height while rotating your palms back towards your body.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining control throughout the movement.
tips: Avoid arching your back; keep your spine neutral.
Keep your movements smooth and controlled to avoid using momentum.
Focus on maintaining the alignment of your elbows and wrists throughout the exercise.
results.description: Dumbbell Kneeling Arnold Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Shoulders.

results.name: Dumbbell Lateral to Front Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms at your sides and palms facing your body.
Lift the dumbbells laterally to shoulder height, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
From the lateral position, move the dumbbells forward until they are directly in front of you, keeping them at shoulder height.
Lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to protect your joints.
Keep your shoulders down and back to avoid straining your neck.
Use a weight that allows you to perform the exercise with proper form.
results.description: Dumbbell Lateral to Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug
instructions: Lie on your right side on a 30 degree incline bench with your knees bent. Hold a dumbbell in your right hand using a neutral grip and let your arm hang straight toward the floor.
Keep your arm straight and raise your working shoulder toward your ear, lifting the dumbbell slightly upward.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back while keeping your torso still.
Slowly lower your shoulder until your arm hangs fully extended, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Keep the side of your torso firmly supported on the incline bench.
Keep your elbow straight and avoid curling the dumbbell.
Pause briefly at the top, then lower your shoulder slowly through the full range of motion.
Exhale as you raise your shoulder and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Laying 30 Degree Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Laying Silverback Shrug
instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest supported, your legs extended, and your feet firmly on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with an overhand grip and let your arms hang straight below your shoulders.
Shrug your shoulders toward your ears and slightly backward while keeping your arms straight and your chest against the bench.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your upper back muscles.
Slowly lower your shoulders to the starting position, allowing them to fully relax before repeating.
tips: Keep your chest firmly supported on the bench throughout the exercise.
Move your shoulders upward and slightly backward without rolling them.
Avoid swinging the dumbbells or using momentum to lift them.
Exhale as you raise your shoulders and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Dumbbell Laying Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Leaning Fly
instructions: Sit on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, with your arms hanging down by your sides and feet flat on the floor.
Lean your torso slightly forward, keeping your back straight. Raise both arms out to your sides at shoulder height, maintaining a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells down to your sides and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled movement.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows to protect your joints.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you bring the dumbbells across your body and inhaling as you extend them back out.
results.description: Dumbbell Leaning Fly is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation
instructions: Lie on your side on the floor with your knees slightly bent for stability. Support your head with your lower hand. Hold a dumbbell in your top hand, keeping your upper arm against your side and your elbow bent at 90 degrees.
Start with your forearm across your abdomen, perpendicular to the floor.
Rotate your shoulder to lift the dumbbell, bringing your forearm to a vertical position without moving your upper arm away from your side.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position, maintaining control throughout the movement.
tips: Keep your upper arm stationary against your side to isolate the shoulder rotation.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to avoid momentum and ensure proper muscle activation.
Use a light weight to start with, as this exercise targets small stabilizing muscles.
results.description: Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Lie face down on a flat bench with your legs bent and forefeet firm on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in one hand, letting it hang straight down from your shoulder and your free hand holding the bench for support.
Keeping your elbow slightly bent, raise the dumbbell out to the side and up to shoulder level, squeezing your shoulder blade at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower the dumbbell back to the starting position in a controlled manner. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Avoid using momentum; focus on a slow and controlled movement.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbow throughout the exercise to reduce joint strain.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift the dumbbell and inhaling as you lower it.
results.description: Dumbbell Lying One Arm Rear Lateral Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.
